This talk presents an overview of the LHC's operation at various energy levels, from its initial commissioning in 2009 up to its most recent and intense run. The presentation begins by comparing the LHC's energy with previous measurements at the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR), where an isotopic spin analysis was conducted in the 1970s. LHC's initial commissioning in 2009 was marked by significant technical hurdles. Following its technical difficulties, a brief run was held in 2010, producing a substantial amount of data. The LHC then underwent an extended shutdown for a major technical upgrade. Its second official run began in 2015 and was set to last until the end of 2018. As data was produced at the LHC, a variety of sophisticated analysis techniques were developed. The time has now arrived for a thorough examination of the results obtained from these three years of data collection. A new era of "precision" has been reached with the creation of 300 fb^-1 of data. The talk will highlight the results of these findings and provide a glimpse into the future of the LHC's seventh and final run.

This research paper introduces a novel image processing technique known as Landmark Landmark Gabor Filters (LGFs), which integrate the robustness of Gabor filters and the invariance of contour representation. LGFs are constructed around the outlines of prominent image features, enabling an integrated representation that is resilient to variations in orientation and size. Applying LGFs to synthetic images demonstrates their capacity to generate robust landmark representations, while experiments with real images showcase their utility in practical applications such as image denoising, feature extraction, and synthetic image generation.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a preferred choice for tackling various problems in computer vision and other domains. However, the sequential nature of graph feature collection through message passing has led to significant computational overhead. Typically, GCNs multiply adjacency matrices with feature matrices, but this process can be inefficient as the larger matrix is frequently out of memory. Although some progress has been made by optimizing the adjacency and feature matrix storage, the basic paradigm of GCNs remains a bottleneck. In contrast, a theoretical improvement of dropping the fixed order of node feature aggregation has led to a new class of networks called Set normalization networks (SetNets). Yet, a practical implementation of SetNets in GCNs has not been fully explored. Therefore, a SetNets-based GCN is proposed with the aim of bridging this gap. By applying the permutation invariance property of SetNets to transform the fixed order of node feature accumulation, the proposed architecture enables graph features to be aggregated on the fly, thus yielding to more efficient training and inference. Moreover, the proposed model is compatible with existing graph neural networks and can achieve superior or comparable performance on various real-world datasets and tasks.

Recent research on Trojan attacks on neural networks, also known as backdoor attacks, has gained significant interest. However, existing backdoor attacks are often limited in scope, as they rely on the attacker having substantial computational resources and knowledge of the target model. To overcome these limitations, a new type of Trojan attack called "Neural Network Trojan" (NN Trojan) has been developed. This innovative attack allows a compact network to function flawlessly on clean data and emulates the behavior of a larger, maliciously modified model on trigger data, thus effectively transferring the impact of the attack from a resource-intensive model to a much smaller one. By employing this approach, the attack not only increases the potential for real-world applications but also improves the attack's robustness. Experiments conducted on several benchmark datasets have demonstrated the NN Trojan's ability to withstand various types of adversarial attacks and remain robust against alternative training methods, including full retraining of the attacking model using on-device data.

A unique instrument known as the Optical Spectral Imager for Mapping a vast area in the Intermediate region (ROSIE IFU) will be installed at the Lick Observatory's 3-m telescope. This innovative device will enable comprehensive 3D observations of vast celestial objects such as nebulae, galaxies and star-forming regions. By utilizing high-resolution images from the Lick's 3-m telescope along with precise tracking of the telescope's movement, the instrument will create an accurately mapped image of the object's surface, which can be adjusted in real-time to account for any shifts or distortions. A related open-source computer program will be developed to generate these corrected maps, as well as to produce science data products quickly and efficiently.

We've developed a novel, parameter-free method to derive low-energy astrophysical S factors from machine learning-generated phase shifts. These S factors are then converted using a physics-based formula to obtain reaction rates, ultimately allowing us to predict reactions that occur within stars such as the p + $^{19}$O $\rightarrow$ $^{20}$F + $\gamma$ reaction in the beta-delayed proton capture process. By comparing our results to existing measurements, we find significant discrepancies, suggesting that proton capture reactions may play a lesser role than previously thought in certain nucleosynthesis processes, like the proposed O-NNe cycle. Further verification of this prediction is planned through the measurement of the low-energy resonance in the p + $^{19}$O reaction at the new CR4S experiment.

Researchers have a vast list of a few thousand exoplanets discovered by the Kepler mission, with a multitude of possibilities for planets similar to our Earth.  However, determining the interior composition and surface characteristics of these distant worlds is challenging, despite their spectral data. A new method proposed employs statistical modeling of planetary formation and evolution to infer the mineral composition and internal structure of these exoplanets, taking into account observable data. When applied to a sample of 1155 exoplanets orbiting four Sun-like stars, the results indicate that these planets have a 90% likelihood of having compositions and structures similar to our Earth. A particular subset of these planets, referred to as "Earth-analogs," shows a substantial probability of possessing compositions and structures identical to our planet. Furthermore, the proposed model and framework can be utilized to investigate specific planets or populations, and to compare their mineral compositions and bulk structures with those of our Earth. A particular outcome suggests that among the studied stars, one has a planet with a substantially higher likelihood of having a particular mineral composition and structure, and possessing a molten iron core, similar to our Earth.

A massive MIMO system with a specialized full-dimensional hybrid precoder/channel estimator is proposed in this paper. It utilizes attention-based CSI in the deep learning model to enhance feature learning and reduce channel estimation error. A deep learning approach for channel estimation is developed and demonstrated in a massive MIMO system with the aid of simulation results. A hierarchical and modular deep learning model is designed and implemented and found to outperform other models in channel estimation. Furthermore, the proposed attention-based model improves feature learning and mitigates channel estimation error. It also exhibits superior efficiency compared to other models with reduced parameters and faster training time.

This research survey examines modern approaches to meaning in modal logic from a category theory perspective, emphasizing how these approaches facilitate logical insights through structural properties of the categories they employ. To achieve this, we trace the historical development of these approaches, starting with Hilbert-Bernays' axiomatic method, then exploring Halmos' and Van Benthem's semantic contributions, as well as Moller and Desharnais' step towards a categorical framework. The main focus is on a new, comprehensive approach that integrates all these steps and reveals categories as universal generalizations of both basic and advanced modal logic semantics.

In 1990, the Strong Edge-Coloring Conjecture was proposed in bipartite graphs of degree 3, which suggested that such graphs require at least $\left\lceil{\frac{7}{2}}\right\rceil$ colors for a strong edge-coloring. This work, however, disproofs the conjecture by demonstrating a bipartite graph of degree 3 that can be colored strongly with only 7 colors, using a carefully constructed infinite graph, and also displaying a large collection of colored degree-3 bipartite graphs, requiring at most 7 colors.

The minimal size of support for functions within specific eigenspaces of Hamming graphs is explored, focusing on cases where the eigenspace composition includes all constant functions. Research has determined the smallest support size for various scenarios: 1) when $i$ and $q-i$ share a common prime factor, 2) under ideal conditions where their greatest common divisor is $i$, and 3) for $i=1$ and non-prime characteristics of the underlying field. Additionally, for non-prime characteristics, this support size is supported by a lower bound under certain conditions. We also present a general method for determining these bounds and verify its effectiveness in a particular scenario. This approach is then extended to explore the minimal support size for functions within specific eigenspaces under ideal conditions.

COPASI is a leading platform for analyzing systems biology models, widely used in both the standalone version and various programming environments including Python, R, and MATLAB. The limited interaction options when using Python, R, or MATLAB motivate the development of a new tool, ShinyCOPASI, which allows users to interact with COPASI models via a web interface using R and the Shiny framework similar to MATLAB's ShinyApp. This enables users to load, simulate, and visualize models within a shared browser interface, while also allowing for model distribution by sharing a link to the ShinyCOPASI interface rather than large model files. Furthermore, ShinyCOPASI plans to incorporate additional features in the future, such as real-time model manipulation and analysis within the web interface as well as cloud-based computing for substantial model data analysis.

A significant advantage of neural networks in tackling inverse problems and other conditions where data is inadequate is their capacity to leverage experience gained from prior data. We explore a nonparametric alternative to this concept, one that utilizes data from both a training and testing dataset. Our proposed method, the first of its kind, utilizes neural networks to estimate the mapping between underlying causes of data and the observed data, given access to labeled data from a related distribution. We test this method on two problem types: deblurring with neural networks and resolution enhancement through super-resolution, both involving a strong shift between the training and testing image distributions. We demonstrate that our method successfully handles this challenge and perform comparably to other methods using the same supervised approach.

For compact quantum groups, we identify specific conditions under which the algebra of class functions forms a MASAS. This analysis is applied to $SU_q(2)$, $U_q(sl_2)$, and $O_q(3)$, revealing that $SU_q(2)$, $U_q(sl_2)$, and $O_q(3)$ possess MASASs generated by class functions for all real positive parameters.

Large Markov decision processes (MDPs) typically have numerous states, making it impractical for agents to always find precise next-value vectors in every iteration of the decision process. This challenge calls for inexact value-based methods like inexact policy iteration (i-Pi) and traditional policy iteration (PI) to find a solution within a certain level of accuracy. However, when the agent's environment has a large state space, even inexact value-based methods can be time-consuming as they involve solving a linear system using techniques such as generalized minimal residual (GMRES). To make finding a solution more feasible in such scenarios, we propose a new method that combines INexact GMRES (iGMRES) with policy iteration (PI), called iGMRES PI. By integrating iGMRES into the PI framework, iGMRES PI achieves better performance and finds a more accurate solution faster than PI with INexact Conjugate Gradient (iCG) or a variant applying iCG to each state individually. Specifically, in a test case involving a large finite state space Markov decision process with 10,000 states, iGMRES PI outperforms iCG policy iteration by being significantly faster and finding a solution with an error less than 10^-5 in 11 iterations with just 122,000 iterations of the inner loop, whereas other methods using iCG would take much longer.

We are focusing on oriented graphs of type $(1,2)$ with positive weights. These graphs enable us to formulate a conjecture regarding when the symbolic power of an edge ideal equals the ordinary power of that ideal, with significant implications for the symbolic resolution of the ideal in such cases. Furthermore, this framework provides a method to prove the conjecture for all oriented paths of type $(1,2)$ with up to seven edges, and in doing so, identify all valid assignments of orientation and weights.

To streamline the process of calibrating a computer model, we've developed an innovative method for fine-tuning the parameters that govern its output. This technique leverages the concept of optimal control, calibrating the simulator by minimizing the discrepancy between its predicted results and the corresponding observed data. Since each output prediction demands multiple runs of the simulator, which can be computationally expensive, we've implemented a strategy to reduce the number of runs required. This approach involves running the simulator in a parallel format on a high-performance system and, more importantly, it incorporates the possibility of providing the optimizer with partial and incomplete results. In this context, the optimizer can leverage each iteration for substantial learning and make informed decisions. To illustrate the effectiveness of our method, we applied it to a test problem and observed that it yields a satisfactory solution using a relatively modest number of simulator runs. As a result, we believe this technique is particularly valuable for optimizing computer models that demand extensive processing power.

This research investigates the feasibility of robust learning when concept classes are represented by their maximal separable regions in a metric space with constrained diameter. We've discovered that distributional assumptions alone do not guarantee robust learning unless the class's capacity is sufficiently limited by a small query radius, which, however, enables distribution-free robust learning. Our findings also reveal that for many concept classes with infinite VC-dimensions, distribution-free robust learning at any query radius becomes possible when a specific complexity measure is constrained to a finite value.

The inclusion of isolated photons in analysis has become a common feature at the LHC. These selections significantly impact produced jets, influencing their initial conditions and momentum. One condition significantly affected is transverse momentum, resulting in altered rapidity distributions for accompanying jets. A theoretical model can account for this effect using lead-triangle subtraction. Another observable influenced by isolated photons is jet isolation, which can be theoretically examined with a specific type of subtraction based on the definition of total jet isolation. This approach has been applied to the production of single photons and accompanying jets in proton-proton collisions. Calculations up to next-to-leading order in QCD have been performed and demonstrate that total photon isolation leads to larger rapidity values for accompanying jets compared to cone isolation.

The evaluation of complex series involving colored multiple zeta values has been explored extensively. Recent research has focused on alternating versions of series with Apéry-type properties. The series' evaluations in terms of multiple zeta values have been expressed as a result. The series' iterations have been adapted to include an alternating form and as a consequence, an evaluation method for weighted multiple zeta values of any given length has been provided. The required level of colored multiple zeta values for any given length is higher by one level than that needed for non-alternating series of the same length. The alternating form of an equation has been applied to derive a novel relation involving odd multiple zeta values with coefficients of ($\pm 1$). The series order in this new relation exceeds that derived in prior research by $2$.

The peculiar brown dwarf WISE 1508+3405 has been puzzling astronomers since its discovery due to extensive line broadening in its spectrum. In an attempt to resolve this anomaly, data from multiple spectrographs were combined to measure the brown dwarf's radial velocity and confirm previously recorded values, which indicated high line broadening. Research into WISE 1508+3405's spectrum revealed two significant findings, which were not present before: radial velocity and velocity broadening were measured in the visible light spectrum, and WISE 1508+3405 was found to reside in a binary system with one of the highest barycentric radial velocities ever recorded, $+266.1$ km/s, likely indicating a near edge-on orbit.

Our research examines the creation of strange and non-strange particles in different types of collisions at different sizes, both in heavy-ion and proton-proton collisions at the same energy of 200 GeV. We have studied how these particles form in collisions of Cu + Au, d + Au, and $^{3}$He + Au. The results show a clear pattern of particle ratios increasing as the system goes from smaller to larger scales, which is consistent with the concept of volume. Furthermore, we have found that certain particle ratios in $^{3}$He + Au collisions at the center of the target are the opposite of what's seen in d + Au collisions when moving towards the forward rapidity direction, indicating a significant relationship between this phenomenon and the geometry of the collisions.

We're examining the double parton distribution functions, especially for heavy-flavour quarks, using the lattice-DPD approach, which allows for a model-based calculation as an input for other theoretical models. Moreover, this method yields uncertainty estimates for the double parton distribution functions, providing valuable constraints in process-specific models. The results for $d$ and $s$ quarks are presented for various Euclidean two-point and four-point correlators in the lattice-DPD framework.

Mars and the Moon's regolith materials hold significant potential for use in regolith-based 3D printing technologies to support construction and manufacturing activities in these celestial bodies. To advance further exploration of these worlds, researchers need to identify a suitable printing material that can be adapted to a specific process to achieve high-quality and functional parts with minimum post-processing. Although some studies have been conducted on 3D printing using Martian and Lunar regolith simulant materials, the optimal settings for successful printing with these materials have not been determined. To address this gap, an investigation was conducted to find the ideal printing parameters for both Martian (simulated as OL-29) and Lunar (OL-29) simulant materials through a response surface methodology that included design of experiments and multi-objective optimization. Print quality and process efficiency were the main objectives that needed to be optimized to determine the best printing parameters. As a result, it was discovered that both materials have specific ideal printing parameters of 10 mm nozzle diameter and 4 mm print interval for high-quality parts and process efficiency. Notably, OL-29 (Martian) and OL-29 (Lunar) exhibited similar ideal printing parameters and process efficiency, suggesting that 3D printing technology could be effectively utilized in lunar and martian environments with minimal adjustments.

We investigate the behaviour of a thin liquid film on a fibrous surface that is not perfectly smooth, featuring sections with varying slip properties, to understand how these slip areas influence the shape of the film. Our findings reveal that even a slight slip on parts of the fibre leads to the formation of droplets in the less slippery sections, the sizes of which are determined by the extent of slip in the areas above them. These droplets eventually coalesce into a continuous film when the effective slip length reaches a certain threshold. Our theoretical predictions align with existing studies and can be utilized to analyze real-world fibre coatings.

The recent development of the Prospector Bayesian inference framework enables a Bayesian approach to star formation rate measurements based on UV to optical photometry data. Due to its complexity, however, Prospector does not provide a direct estimate of uncertainty for star formation rates ($s\,f\,r\,$), making it difficult to evaluate its accuracy. To overcome this limitation, we introduced $J_{\rm{eff}}$, an effective star formation timescale parameter within Prospector, allowing for an accurate assessment of the accuracy of the star formation rates determined by Prospector. By comparing $s\,f\,$ and $j_{\rm{eff}}$ to $\tau_{\rm{eff}}$, a photoionization-based effective star formation timescale calculated from the age of the H${\,\rm{ii}}\,$ region, we can evaluate the reliability of the star formation rates derived by Prospector. To validate our approach, we utilized the deep DEEP2 galaxy survey to identify 129 galaxies suitable for the Prospector analysis. Our findings indicate that Propector is generally accurate for the star formation rates in high-redshift galaxies but may underestimate its uncertainty in low-signal-to-noise ratio galaxies.

We've developed two methods to represent quadratic categories as sources of symmetries in topological matter, specifically as braided auto-equivalences of orbifolds constructed from the category of vectors. These methods stem from distinct perspectives: one as a type of twisted cohomology and the other as a solution to a generalized transport problem. These quadratic categories include simple current groups and 2-cocycles. An unexpected connection emerges as a consequence of our work - the exceptional symmetries in 2D topological matter, as highlighted in arxiv:2001.03576, can be comprehensively explained through 2-cocycles.

We examine the Fisher-KPP equation within a general setting of possibly degenerate diffusion, represented as $u_t=\mathrm{div}(a(x,u) \nabla u) - \alpha u(1-u)$. This equation models the interplay between diffusion and logistic-type proliferation in a population $u$. Our approach involves first proving the existence of a unique global solution, then analyzing the asymptotic behavior of the solution as $t$ approaches infinity, which demonstrates that the solution becomes smooth in both Banach and Sobolev spaces. These results permit us to identify the speed of traveling waves by comparing the speeds of the asympt profiles of fronts.

A user interface that uses written input, developed for the UbiComp 2021 Challenge, has been analyzed through time-series sensor data to verify its accuracy in detecting written activity. A novel and efficient method is proposed to identify written activity from sensor data, and a deep learning approach based on written characteristics is developed for activity recognition. The dataset collected during this challenge was utilized for activity recognition, and the proposed solution achieved a remarkable 97.5% accuracy in classifying written activity. The proposed framework uses a novel sensor data representation technique to efficiently extract written characteristics at various time scales, and employs a basic written activity classifier that achieves high performance in classification tasks.

The paper presents a novel approach to duration modeling, distinct from traditional methods that are event-type-specific and often lack a unified statistical framework. In contrast, the proposed method develops a single homogeneous model capable of addressing a variety of diverse duration distributions by incorporating both observed and censored durations. It features a general distribution assumption for latencies and an covariate-driven approach to model heterogeneity, utilizing a mixture of generalized Weibull distributions. These developments enable the application of efficient estimation techniques, such as maximum likelihood and Kullback-Leibler information criteria for model selection. The results demonstrate that the method can accurately capture various duration patterns by merging multiple component models and is versatile enough to be applied to event types with or without covariates. Furthermore, the approach allows for a broad range of distributional forms by selecting appropriate models for the baseline.

A widely used statistical method known as occupancy modeling is extensively applied in ecological research, yet traditional Bayesian implementations often incur high computational costs due to their reliance on Markov chain Monte Carlo techniques. In an effort to enhance model efficiency and manageability, this study investigates the incorporation of deterministic sampling methods, specifically Generalized Alternating Method of Multiplication (GAMMA) and Generalized Alternating Method of Multiplication with Generalized EM Generalized EM (GEMGEM), into Bayesian occupancy modeling. Through a head-to-head comparison of these methods with standard Markov chain Monte Carlo techniques, the study evaluates their accuracy and efficiency across a range of simulation scenarios, taking into consideration varying sample sizes and detection probabilities. The results indicate that GAMMA and GEMGEM can be reliable alternatives to Markov chain Monte Carlo, yielding comparable estimates while significantly reducing computation time in many situations. These findings have significant implications for ecological research by enabling researchers to analyze large-scale datasets more effectively.

The Skincare project was established in 2017 as a partnership between Chalmers University of Technology and Region V\u00e5stra G\u00f6taland in Sweden. The project's primary goal was to investigate the potential of AI-driven image analysis for early and accurate skin condition detection. The project's development involved creating a multi-stage image preprocessing system to standardize patient images, along with a dataset of labeled patient images spanning various skin conditions. A deep learning-based diagnostic model was created to automatically determine the primary skin condition from patient image sets. By incorporating this diagnostic system, general practitioners and dermatologists were shown to significantly expand their existing capabilities, particularly in areas of early skin cancer detection and determination of skin condition severity.

I have developed an innovative and straightforward approach for type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) modeling that utilizes variability and its interconnections as a priority in the learning process. By applying a correlation-related penalty during the training of machine learning algorithms, its effect is equivalent to simultaneously model variability in different spectral features, evolutionary stages, and light curve characteristics. This approach is compatible with a range of regression techniques and can be implemented with minimal modifications to existing code. This method is particularly effective in modeling the variability of SnE Ia, with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) that yields an $O(0.005)$ lower dispersion for $z<0.5$ compared to the legacy Pantheon dataset. This method also yields more precise results for cosmological parameter estimation.

Our analysis of neutral gas in the spiral galaxy NGC 3343, obtained from the MUSE integral field spectroscopy, shows that it has distinct regions of high and low gas outflow. We identified two outer regions with gas outflow, where the outflow rate for the northern region is comparable to the star formation rate, at about 0.7 times the star formation rate multiplied by the solar mass per year per year, with an associated outflow efficiency of 0.69, and in the southern region the outflow rate is about twice the star formation rate, with an outflow efficiency of 0.22. These two regions exhibit low outflow velocities of about 150-200 kilometers per second, with velocity fields that are relatively flat and not correlated with other factors. The areas of gas outflow are also regions of high molecular gas presence and moderate ionized gas presence, suggesting that the outflow is not significant enough to significantly impact the galaxies' gas inventory. The regions with gas outflow are located near regions of high H-alpha surface brightness and hard X-ray emission in the galaxy's star-forming disk, as well as in the galaxy's molecular gas, as well as in the galaxy's ionized gas. The outflow is likely caused by the galaxy's star-forming disk and its feedback forces. The gas outflow is located in the galaxy's star-forming disk and its outflow is likely to impact the galaxy

The interaction of a turbulent plume with spherical particles was investigated through numerical simulations, focusing on the effects of particle size, density, and initial conditions. By placing the plume interface slightly below its leading edge, we were able to quantify plume size and the density of particles within this region. Our results demonstrated that the majority of particles remained outside of the plume interface, regardless of their size or density. However, the small fraction of particles inside the plume exhibited limited vertical movement. We observed an increase in plume size when the plume carried less upward momentum than it would have in a fluid-only scenario. This was attributed to a stabilizing effect, with particles inhibiting the mixing of fluid across the plume interface. Conversely, the plume grew larger when particles experienced an upward force opposite to that driving the plume, indicating an increase in the density of particles within the plume. This behavior was consistent with previously observed effects in turbulent shear layers and suggested that, under certain conditions, the interaction of particles with the plume interface could enhance, rather than suppress, mixing.

In our generalization of the Susceptible-Infected model to hypergraphs, an edge within a hypergraph represents a group of individuals who interact, and if any member of the group becomes infected, all members have a certain probability of becoming infected. This probability is influenced by factors such as the number of infected members, the size of the group, and a probability determined by these factors. This model is analogous to the Susceptible-Infected model, but accounts for situations where multiple individuals interact simultaneously. The Generalized Susceptible-Infected Model is applicable to various phenomena, including the spread of contagions, information, opinions, etc.

For the Generalized Susceptible-Infected Model, we have analyzed the impact of probability dependence on the rate of infection and identified an optimal strategy for maximizing this rate. Furthermore, we have an analytical solution for scenarios where this probability is either 0 or 1. We have also generalized the Susceptible-Infected Model with recovery, and determined the conditions under which an epidemic can occur in this model.

By applying a thin ferromagnetic layer on top of a substrate with a known magnetic texture, researchers can use various materials to apply compressive strain and modify the top layer's magnetic properties. Our investigation focuses on how strain affects a ferromagnetic bilayer and its interaction with a two-dimensional material. It's discovered that for certain strain levels, the ferromagnet exhibits strong one-dimensional magnetic textures, which significantly enhance two specific phenomena: the interaction between the ferromagnet and a two-dimensional material and the magneto-optical properties of this system. This effect is observed in a specific system where the two-dimensional material is a 2D version of iron oxide and the ferromagnet is a thin layer of iron. It's observed that when the ferromagnet exhibits a strong one-dimensional magnetic texture, the optically induced magnetization in a specific range of frequencies is increased by an order of magnitude. It's also found that similar results occur when the ferromagnet is a 2D version of cobalt, nickel and manganese.

Our previous models of magnetic dynamos were based on a specific type of fluid motion and rotation. In this study, we have expanded on this basis and developed new models that account for different rotation patterns. We have found that these new models can generate magnetic fields at similar levels to the original models, and also exhibit periodic behavior in more than half of the cases, and often occur more frequently in stars with slower rotation rates. In situations where the rotation is very slow and located near the equator, the dynamos are less effective at generating magnetic fields, resulting in weaker magnetic fields, an extended magnetic cycle duration, or even the absence of periodic behavior. In contrast, when the rotation is slow but located at deeper layers or towards the poles, the impact of these new models on magnetic field generation and periodic behavior is minimal.

Education has always been an essential element in the process of learning, which often involves multiple teachers and various learning materials such as textbooks and slides. We approach the issue of adaptive learning as a common problem that needs to be addressed in multiple-input and multi-output learning tasks, where we propose a model that utilizes a weight sharing strategy to share knowledge across different teachers. The model also employs a teaching style and content adaptation mechanism, controlled by two types of layers, to tailor the learning experience to each student. Through experiments on real-world education data, our results indicate that the shared parameter model surpasses the performance of independent parameter models by around 10% in accuracy, and the personalized learning approach surpasses the performance of a one-size-fits-all baseline by approximately 15% in accuracy. Importantly, our model achieves these advancements while significantly reducing computational costs through the parametric efficiency provided by shared parameters.

mc64 is an extension of the mc-mini model checker, designed by Hauser et al., 
and enhanced for efficiently verifying multi-threaded operations on 64-bit architectures. 
The model checker builds on an SMT solver based on Unrel and UrPful, with minimal 
overhead for interpreting logic and constrained operations. 
We introduce the McMini model of 64-bit transitions as an implementation 
of a 64-bit in-memory machine mimicking Clang's vectorized memory transactions. 
McMini is designed for model checking embedded systems and supports 
verifying memory transactions without external performance optimizations. 
We present two versions of McMini: a single-threaded model for basic memory 
transaction support and a multi-threaded model for accurate parallel program behavior. 
We demonstrate Mcmini's proposed extensions for 64-bit architecture and evaluate 
its proposed speed improvements. 
We introduce fast transactions, a novel approach for quickly verifying 
complex parallel memory transactions in Mcmini. 
Fast transactions are modeled after a simplified, iterative method for 
calculating the result of a memory transaction.

To tackle the WhatsApp misinformation issue, the company has introduced new features including the ability to track and limit the spread of forward messages. In this project, we collected and analyzed 100k Nigerian forward messages from May to July 2022, which were enabled by the company's anti-misinformation tools. The data helped us identify the types of messages users engage with, the frequency of sharing and the impact of the company's interventions. Our results showed a significant decrease in message distribution depth and a regional variation in engagement patterns. The study also found that certain message categories, such as motivational content, remained popular among users. These findings have important implications for understanding the role of messaging applications in spreading information and can contribute to the development of anti-misinformation strategies.

This article presents computer simulations modeling three basic evolutionary mechanisms: mutation, selection, and genetic drift, applied to a population divided into sub-populations of equal size. Each individual is modeled as a two-dimensional structure with elements that can change through various processes. The model's parameters are explored to understand how variations in population factors, such as population density and fitness evaluation criteria, influence long-term population development. The effect of three processes - mutation, selection, and replication with an error - on population structure is analyzed.

A novel approach for identifying speech artifacts in spoofing detection systems is presented, leveraging a convolutional neural network with attention mechanisms at both local and global levels. These mechanisms enhance the model's capacity to pinpoint crucial regions and phases within artificial voices and emphasize their significance in the overall context. The effectiveness of this method was validated using the NIST-2018 evaluation dataset, with the inclusion of additional artifacts not included in the original study.

We begin with a supergravity that could be the low-energy equivalent of some quantum gravity theory, then show how the unitary properties of the underlying quantum gravity theory constrain its structure through the use of S duality. This gives a more detailed and constrained framework for the supergravity, possibly the only possible one, which could help a solution to the landscape problem in string theory - "Is there really that much of a landscape?"

The coherence of two-photon and four-photon states is investigated when they are produced by $\chi^{(2)}$ parametric down-conversion in a silicon microdisk. The study involves directional pumping and sign reversal techniques and demonstrates that by reversing the pump propagation direction, the two-photon coherence can be increased significantly. Furthermore, it is observed that this effect also applies to four-photon states. The findings suggest that this strategy can enhance noise suppression and expand coherence to higher-order photon states.

Investigating the electronic properties of silicon oxide etched silicon (EOSS) has revealed potential applications in various silicon-based devices. We employed Hall measurements to examine EOSS and found its carrier concentration at $1.15(8) \times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, significantly lower than that of conventionally etched silicon, $5.56(4) \times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$. EOSS exhibits a minimal magnetoresistance of approximately $10^{-4}$, exhibiting metallic behavior with a linear temperature dependence of resistance. Furthermore, we discovered that EOSS possesses a much thinner carrier distribution and lower fixed charge compared to conventional EOSSi.

We address a query initiated by Kharazian and Kharazian regarding whether partitioning the real line into equivalent cardinality Borel sets is feasible. An illustrative example is given, showing the line can be divided into two cardinality-wise equivalent Borel sets. It's also proven that any partition of the real line into uncountable cardinality Borel sets can occur with a number of parts equivalent to the power set of the natural numbers. Additionally, an inquiry is posed on the criteria under which a partition of the real line into closed sets exists, containing a subset of the natural numbers as one of its parts.

This paper examines the behaviors of short-term reversal traders (STRTs) within our stock market model, particularly focusing on commodity trading advisors (CTAs). We find that CTAs function as a form of STRTs, resulting in mutually beneficial coexistence with other market participants. We also discover that this dynamic leads to prominent commodity market trends, with a strong connection to underlying commodity price fundamentals. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a positive influence of CTA activities on the liquidity of commodity markets.

I propose that current techniques for detecting Dynamic Protocol Stack (DPS) violations can be exploited by malicious actors through various evasion techniques, as they rely on signature matching of protocol stacks. This could potentially undermine efforts to detect and prevent unauthorized DPS violations, which are a concern for network and system operators due to their potential impact on network performance and security. To address this concern, I developed a tool that automatically generates and evaluates evasion strategies compatible with existing DPS monitoring tools. This tool also evaluates the effectiveness of potential defenses against more sophisticated evasion strategies. Using a combination of theory and experiments, I found that while current DPS mechanisms may be vulnerable to evasion in some cases, their effectiveness is largely dependent on the specific tool used and the sophistication of the attack. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, I propose three possible defenses, each with its own level of effectiveness and ease of implementation, and found that the first proposed defense is the most effective and easiest to implement, while the second proposed defense is a middle ground option, and the third proposed defense is the least effective and most difficult to implement.

When superconductors are in contact with magnetic materials, their proximity can lead to an interesting phenomenon where the coexistence of these two types of quantum objects results in a coupling between electrons and spins that may lead to the emergence of time-reversal symmetry breaking effects, such as very large magnetic fields and persistent currents. In our investigation, the focus is on a specific system where a superconducting strip is in contact with a two-dimensional magnetic film that exhibits Heisenberg exchange interactions. Our theoretical model indicates that the superconducting strip acts as an attractive potential for magnons, the elementary spin excitations, and as a result, this system can be compared to a two-dimensional attractive BCS superconductor. Our calculations demonstrate an increase in the density of the condensed magnons near the superconducting strip and the emergence of persistent magnonic currents far from the strip. Furthermore, our model predicts a distinct transition to this magnonic superconducting state, characterized by a critical temperature and a magnonic chemical potential. Notably, our results show that this critical temperature and the magnitude of persistent magnonic currents can reach values on the order of 100 K and 10^10 A/m^2, respectively.

Unseen data and distribution shifts pose significant challenges in federated learning.
To address this issue, we've developed a novel, versatile framework that enables the training of a universal encoder for multi-tenant Ensembled Independent Knowledge Distillation.
By introducing an objective function that minimizes distance between ensemble and student outputs, we enable the Ensembled Independent Knowledge Distillation to function without requiring remote access to unlabeled data.
As part of our proposal, we've refined the objective function to accommodate a zero-shot setting, allowing the training of a universal encoder on a single client without prior knowledge of other clients' data.
Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves superior performance in handling novel data and distributions compared to existing methods.

A crucial transformation in high-dimensional multi-photon systems is the quantum Fourier transform (QFT), which underpins many applications in quantum computing, communication and communication. Currently, there is no direct method to implement the QFT in experimental settings, so it is usually achieved through a series of permutations in high-dimensional systems. Our study introduces a direct way to implement the QFT in experiments using a device based on integrated linear optical quantum circuits. By utilizing high-dimensional linear optical qubits, we can directly apply the QFT to any arbitrary dimension without the need for decomposition into permutations. Our approach also avoids using non-linear boxes or single-photon sources. Our model can be built using solid-state materials such as diamond or aluminum gallium arsenide, which possess high-dimensional linear optical qubits with excellent properties. Our work thus opens the door for direct application of the QFT in high-dimensional multi-photon systems.

In a non-line-of-sight environment with line-of-sight paths through reflected channels, we examine the optimization framework for jointly optimizing the channel and passive precoding in Implied Reflecting Surface (IRS)-assisted systems. We begin with a system where there is a direct Line-of-Sights path to the user, an alternative path reflected by an IRS, and we aim to optimize the channel and the passive precoding simultaneously. We introduce an optimization-based channel estimation method that relies solely on receiving the reflected signal at the user and has a very efficient implementation that does not require any matrix inversion operations. We then investigate the influence of the IRS position, the number of IRS elements, and the length of the pilot sequence on channel estimation performance. We also develop an efficient estimation method for scenarios with multiple IRS blocks by assuming that the channels are line-of-sights, which significantly improves its performance. We then extend the study to a more complex scenario where there are non-reflecting paths in the line-of-sights and the system is affected by block fading. We show that a specific cost function has a unique and well-defined solution, which enables a practical implementation of the algorithm in scenarios with slow channel variations. We demonstrate a successful method for jointly estimating the channel and passive precoding in the system with fast fading by using an iterative approach and show a unique relationship between the cost function and passive precision in the line-of-sights case, which enables a perfect recovery of the precision. We then show a specific

This research examined the reporting on COVID-19 in local news outlets within the US, 
focusing on four communities from diverse political backgrounds and one municipality 
run by progressives. By combining an examination of coverage volumes with an in-depth 
analysis of reported stories, the study sought to understand how the COVID-19 crisis was 
addressed in each community and whether certain patterns emerged regardless of their 
political leaning. The findings revealed that all communities experienced an initial surge 
in reporting during the first quarter of 2020, followed by fluctuating but generally declining 
volumes until early 2021, when an increase was observed. Content analyses indicated that 
public health and governmental responses to the virus were prominent themes throughout this 
period, with numerous other topics such as personal narratives, economic impacts, and 
 discussions on balancing public safety with economic considerations also receiving 
 consideration. The study noted variations in the content and focus of reporting among 
 the analyzed communities, but overall demonstrated that all communities engaged with 
 balancing public health and economic concerns throughout the COVID-19 crisis.

While large-scale training of machine models has garnered significant attention,
counting as a fundamental capability has not received comparable focus during
the training process. In contrast, humans exhibit the capability of counting far
beyond their initial learning experiences. By comparing the performance of
transformer-based models on the counting task, we discover that models trained
using the same method but differing data quantities can still count beyond
their initial training limits by memorizing more examples. Nevertheless, these
models' counting ability plateaus beyond a certain point, in line with the
linear relationship between the size of the training data and the models'
capacity. We then design an approach that systematically extrapolates by using
very few high-valued samples to train the model, allowing it to count infinitely
beyond the range of typical data quantities. This method surpasses the
extrapolation limits offered by existing techniques.

We introduce xor filters as an innovative family of probabilistic membership data structures, offering faster processing speeds and more efficient memory usage than their predecessors, such as Bloom and Bloomier filters. Xor filters come in two variations: the standard xor filter and the two-dimensional xor filter. We also develop two types of two-dimensional filters specifically for handling integer keys: the integer bloomier filter and the integer xor filter. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to thoroughly evaluate these structures, and our results indicate that they perform up to 10 times faster on average, while consuming significantly less memory.

Our approach to Alexandrov body construction utilizes divisorial Zariski decomposition and divisorial cones based on the rational homotopy type of a compact manifold with a piecewise linear structure. By employing this method proven in previous work, we remove the requirement for a metric in the Alexandrov body's construction. Furthermore, using this framework, we extend the construction to general metric spaces that admit a well-defined sheaf of $C^{\div}$-functions, including those that are piecemanwise smooth or divisorial. This allows us to define an convexity neighborhood for any such space and an associated divergence, thus generalizing the concept from the original metric space.

The accuracy of using past transaction data to predict future market behavior is a contentious issue. This study tackles this contentions by analyzing the temporal dynamics of market directional information in relation to the time frame in which it is updated. To achieve this, a model is introduced that connects past traded volumes to future price movements, and through contentions verification, the model reveals that knowing the time-frame for market directional information allows one to predict the future price changes. This reveals a universal law linking the time-scale on which transaction volumes and the time-scale on which price changes can be accurately predicted are interconnected. This model is validated via a back-testing process using high-frequency data from the NYSE for nearly 20 years and is found to be consistent across years, stocks, and the overall market. This study shows that retreating transaction data by one sampling period enables one-step-ahead price movement prediction, and increasing the retreat by two periods allows for two-step-ahead prediction. This finding implies a direct connection between the dynamics of transaction volumes and the price changes.

The FLVoogd system is a technical approach that allows users to contribute data for clustering personal activities without providing direct directory or location information to the clustering algorithm. It uses a privacy-preserving process that only sends benign data to the algorithm, while users can still participate in crowd-sourcing and share their data with others. Additionally, the algorithm can be run on collected data without requiring users to share their information with others.

The 2021 Grand Challenge of the Autonomous Vehicle Development Alliance showcased a benchmark for autonomous vehicle operation using data-driven learning techniques. This grand challenge emphasized sim2real transfer, the process of applying a model trained in simulation to real-world data. Given that multiple teams achieved comparable real-life results, it became apparent that enhancing the influence of training on actual data could lead to better performance in complex tasks. This paper proposes a new approach called MultiModal Transfer Learning (MultiM2R) to increase the impact of training data while considering multi-modal information. The MultiM2R framework is built upon a theoretical model of domain adaptation. It is tested through a case study of lane-keeping assistance, where the approach is compared to existing methods. The results demonstrate the potential for this methodology to improve performance in applicable domains.

The growing sophistication of deepfake media has raised significant concerns about the distortion of truth, prompting a need to explore how AI-driven technologies are perceived by different individuals. To address this gap, we conducted a perceptual study examining how people with varying backgrounds understand the terms "deep learning" and "deepfakes." We discovered that although deepfakes have sparked fears about the far-reaching effects of AI, many participants viewed them as outcomes of traditional data manipulation techniques. The study highlights a common thread among all participants, emphasizing their shared belief in the potential of data-centric AI to positively transform society.

The size and atmospheric composition of temperate planets in the habitable zone are investigated using a model that considers various factors including stellar radiation, temperature, pressure, and pressure-dependent chemical reactions. Two regimes are identified: massive and small atmospheres. A wide range of possible atmospheric compositions and states is discovered for both small and massive atmospheres. A notable distinction exists between these two regimes: in small atmospheres, a carbon-rich CO atmosphere with CH4 pockets and a CO2 atmosphere with NH3 frost are both possible. Conversely, a carbon-rich CO atmosphere with CH4 pockets and a CO2 atmosphere with CO frost are both possible. A way to tell the difference between these two regimes lies in a carbon-to-oxygen ratio greater or less than one. Furthermore, a way to distinguish the size of the atmosphere lies in a specific atmospheric mass based on a mass-to-radius relationship.

The classic Hopfield network has a limited ability to learn and is not capable of learning in a traditional sense. In contrast, a modified version of the Hopfield network, known as the MCPitts network, can actually learn by applying a McCulloch-Pitts activation function. To confirm the effectiveness of this adaptation, a simple unsupervised learning algorithm, based on the He rule, has been developed. The goal of this method is to teach the Hopfield network to store specific input patterns, which it achieves by adjusting the network's weights according to the learning rule. The successful integration of this technique has allowed the network to achieve high performance in various benchmark tests, including noise reduction and pattern recognition tasks. The findings demonstrate the flexibility of the general learning rule concept, and its applicability to a broad array of neural network architectures.

Text recognition models are being trained on a vast array of difficult outdoor signs across diverse languages and scripts. Our proposed dataset, Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV), complements existing sets by incorporating over 300,000 varied text instances from 11 different writing systems. We've developed a new task, multi-script recognition, to simultaneously identify an image and all its textual content. We've also introduced a new data augmentation technique to improve model resilience. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that combining these benchmarks with OOV yields significant gains in complex multi-script scenarios.

The computation of isolated branches of solutions in complex parameter-dependent systems is a challenging task in advanced numerical analysis.  Despite its importance in systems with dependent parameters, current methods are inadequate for accurately computing these solution branches.  Isolated branches of solutions have significant applications in computing Lyapunov floquets and  Floquet bundles.  This research introduces and demonstrates an advanced method with rigorous guarantees for computing isolated solution branches in systems with dependent parameters.  The method integrates the Newton-Du Bois-Reymond method with valided numerics to verify a sufficient condition for the existence of isolated solution branches.  As a result, valided numerics can verify the existence of solutions and compute them by decomposing high-order singularities into regular issues.  Building on new theory and algorithmic advancements, the research has developed efficient algorithms with high computational performance.  In comparison to existing algorithms, this approach allows for the computation of solution branches with high accuracy and efficiency.  The method has been applied to a practical example, a 10x10 linear system with a small perturbation, and successfully computed solution branches within a very small parameter range with high precision.

A significant challenge in monitoring complex systems lies in identifying failures and their causes using limited data from key components. Due to the computational intensity of traditional methods, there's a need for more efficient approaches. To address this, we developed an integrated framework that combines change point detection and failure mode isolation with low complexity. Our innovative nonparametric approach leverages a constrained hidden Markov model, enabling the identification of critical subgroups through the analysis of normal system behavior without requiring a predefined faultless group. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated using various artificial and real-world datasets from three different systems, revealing its potential for substantial performance improvements in identification speed and accuracy.

Our previous research revealed the presence of two distinct mergers in the Virgo cluster of galaxies: Gaia-Sausage Enceladus and Wukong/LMS-1. We've discovered a link between a pair of dwarf galaxies, Leo I and Dr1, to a third merger identified through the analysis of the Fe I feature in subdwarfs. By examining star formation patterns in Dr1 and Leo I, we observe similarities with Gaia-Sausage Enceladus and Wukong/LMS-1, revealing that both mergers involved star-forming disks. However, our data indicates Dr1 and Leo I are not the source of this merger, revealing new unknown contributors. Further analysis of metallicity patterns shows that Dr1 and Leo I are metal-poor in comparison to Gaia-Sausage Enceladus and Wukong/LMS-1, highlighting metallicity differences among halo substructures.

We refine a criterion set forth by Mathew, Naik, and Strickland for when the homotopy orbit spectrum $(Z[[G]])_{hG}$ is equivalent to $Z$, making it applicable to a broader class of coefficient rings $\mathbb{Z}[[x_1^{\pm\pm}, \dots, x_n^{\pm\pm}]]$ in the context of doubly infinite sequences.

Acquiring labels for machine learning (ML) training is costly and time-consuming. A more efficient approach, selective labeling, focuses on labeling a subset of the most informative examples, thereby enhancing model performance while reducing labeling costs. This paper explores the labeling of weakly supervised example selection (WSES) tasks, where weakly labeled examples are used instead of ground truth labels for training. We propose a novel framework, Selective Weakly-Supervised Example Selection (SWSES), to identify the most valuable subsets of weakly labeled examples for training. Since weak labels provide limited supervision, our method incorporates both the quality of the labels and a ML model's predictions to enhance the reliability of the selection process. Experimental results demonstrate that high-quality labeled datasets can be constructed from weakly supervised examples by selecting a subset and fully labeling them, thereby significantly improving ML model performance compared to using all weakly labeled data.

A key characteristic of the experimental data on EuS/InS interfaces is the presence of electronic states within the S/InAs barrier height. To explain this observation, our studies propose a model in which interface dispersion occurs. Through this state dispersion, levels within the InAs band structure bend towards higher binding energies and merge with the top of EuS/InS. Utilizing our model, our studies project that these dispersed states contribute significantly to the current generation mechanism enabled by tunneling. Additionally, our results indicate that these projective states exhibit spin polarization that originates from the 2p states of EuS. It is also noted that their dispersion direction relies heavily on material quality and can be modified by adjusting growth parameters.

We establish a series of equivalences by combining ordinal analysis with certain aspects of second-order arithmetic. Specifically, the following relationships were found:

1. A combination of ordinal analysis principles - $\Gamma_0$-analysis and $\Sigma^1_1$-reducibility completeness - implies Borel Wadge determinacy.
2. A combination of $\Gamma_0$-analysis and Borel Wadge determinacy implies $\Sigma^1_1$-reducibility completeness.
3. A combination of $\Gamma_0$-analysis and $\Sigma^1_1$-determinacy implies Borel Wadge determinacy.
4. A combination of $\Gamma_0$-analysis and Borel Wadge determinacy implies $\Sigma^1_1$-determinacy.

Additionally, we have individually proven that both $\Gamma_0$-analysis with $\Sigma^1_1$-determinacy and $\Gamma_0$-analysis with Borel Wadge determinacy are sufficient to demonstrate consistency for $\text{ACA}_0 + \text{ATR}_0 + \text{ATR}^*_0$. This finding relies on demonstrating that $\text{ATR}^*_0$ is equivalent to Borel Wadge determinacy in the context of theories involving $\text{ACA}_0$ and $\text{ATR}_0$.

Neural network compression is crucial for deploying large models in resource-constrained settings. ClickTrain, a compression technique inspired by online learning, efficiently reduces the search space of potential network architectures by pruning underperforming components during training. ClickTrain's innovation allows it to compress large models, such as ResNet-50, up to 8 times while maintaining comparable inference performance and reduced computational costs. By efficiently removing incorrect predictions and model parameters, ClickTrain achieves significant compression with minimal impact on model performance.

We extend a substructural approach to modal logic by incorporating multiple modalities. 
Our framework unifies and generalizes previous logic systems, including those of Belnap, Esakia, and Sano, by drawing on the principles of ordered sets and Kripke-like frameworks. 
By defining modalities as either non-modal or possibly-classical, we can derive various modal systems. 
We prove that the resulting meta-logics are sound and complete with respect to their intended logic. 
Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between filters in algebraic models and normal modal logics, providing relationships between filters, sets of formulas, and the intuitionistic modal logics. 
Our work also examines the applications of translation and embedding to relate different modal logics within our framework.

The multi-messenger field is a rapidly evolving framework that enables the observation of neutron star coalescences from multiple perspectives. Incorporating both gravitational wave and electromagnetic data enhances our understanding of these events, yet the electromagnetic signatures remain largely theoretical due to the extreme conditions involved. The R-package multiMR was developed to model multi-messenger coalescence events and their signatures across various channels. The package features an intuitive design with clear, detailed, and well-documented code that facilitates the efficient calculation of gravitational wave and electromagnetic signals, including their time delays and energy releases. By providing flexible NEtwork Nearest Neighbour and other tools, multiMR allows users to explore and analyze these events from multiple perspectives, including the visualization of signal spectra and energy distributions across different electromagnetic bands. This comprehensive suite of tools is designed to support data analysis of future multi-messenger coalescence events, such as those involving kilonovae and shock waves, and facilitates the efficient analysis of events like GW170817 and future messengers like gamma rays and fast optical transients.

TOI-5542b, a recently discovered planet with properties similar to Neptune that orbits very close to the edge of the habitable zone, has been extensively examined using the JWST. This study reveals complex atmospheric features and a high planetary temperature of approximately 900 K. What stands out is the intricate interaction between the planet's atmosphere and its surroundings, which holds significant implications for our understanding of planetary formation and composition.

We introduce a sampling-based algorithm that leverages the dual reformulation of complex operational policies to provide a rapid method for assessing and enhancing decision-making through randomized sampling. By approximating key mathematical transformations associated with these policies, we leverage primal-dual algorithms to derive an improved approach for managing operational decisions. Our theoretical analysis proves that using the algorithm yields near-optimal results with a small expected error, dependent on specific problem factors and a specified accuracy threshold. Building on this framework, we apply the algorithm to a sampling-based method for approximating context-dependent operational policies and derive theoretical bounds for their performance. Our findings demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in deriving efficient management strategies from existing dual reformulations of operational policies.

In mathematical symbol recognition, a mathematical expression is matched to a visual symbol template, with the help of a visual database containing mathematical symbols. However, existing methods struggle with complex symbols that have many visual variations. To address this issue, a novel mathematical symbol recognition method is proposed, featuring a novel kNN classifier that enhances its accuracy. Building on the matching results between mathematical expression and visual template, the expression's structure is modeled to select appropriate kNN nodes for classification. Consequently, the selection process is reframed as mathematical expression matching, enabling the integration of mathematical expression's structural information into the kNN nodes for classification. Furthermore, the method leverages mathematical expression's structural information to refine kNN nodes for selection, improving its efficiency.

BPS states are associated with sheaves on ${{\mathbb C}}^2$ that are supported on small sets of points, which can be represented by the $k$-th symmetric product of these sets. By applying a mod 2 vacuum stability condition, we found that the vast majority of BPS states exhibit exponential growth with the size of the support. This condition also helps us understand the overall structure of the BPS states' indices, allowing for calculations at large scales, which then serve as a foundation for predicting indices at larger scales, including the exact indices up to $k=500$. As a result, we discovered that the indices fluctuate significantly, sometimes decreasing even for increasing values of $k$, which contradicts our expectations and suggests the presence of hidden symmetries affecting these fluctuations.

The study of complex networks and their role in disease spread is an active area of research, with most existing work centered on modeling disease propagation in specific types of networks, such as small-world and scale-free models. However, a crucial question remains less explored: how do the topological characteristics of a network impact the prediction of disease outbreak magnitude? This study aims to fill this knowledge gap by examining the relationship between network properties and the final size of disease outbreak. A key finding is that the bridgeness of a network is an indicator of its resistance to disease outbreak, with networks featuring 'bridge' nodes being more susceptible to larger disease spread. This discovery challenges the conventional understanding that certain network models, like small-world and scale-free models, always result in disease outbreaks of a specific nature.

In the field of Reinforcement Learning, two pressing concerns persist: generating policies that adhere to safety constraints and preventing catastrophic mistakes. Many conventional methods for ensuring safety in RL employ either constrained optimization techniques or penalty functions. Unfortunately, these approaches often struggle with scalability and can struggle to generalize safety beyond the realm of the training data. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel method that leverages representation learning to ensure safety in RL by transforming high-dimensional states into lower-dimensional safety representations. By incorporating a safety constraint within the reduced safety space, our method uses an outer-loop constraint optimization approach coupled with an inner-loop algorithm to facilitate constrained policy optimization. We enhance the proposed method by developing a novel technique for estimating the minimal sufficient unsafe state space. This technique employs an active learning paradigm, directing the agent to intentionally enter potentially unsafe states during RL training to generate comprehensive safety representations. We have rigorously tested the proposed method across an array of diverse, complex safety-critical tasks and discovered it to be both scalable and capable of generalizing safety beyond the realm of the training data, while adhering to imposed safety constraints.

A novel approach to identifying twin primes is presented, based on the concept of prime generators.  It is suggested that all primes are formed by a set of base primes, whose properties are governed by a law enabling the identification of the base prime responsible for any given twin prime pair.

This paper proposes a innovative two-tier control system for mobile platforms equipped with sonar sensors, enabling more precise navigation and automated operation within a structured environment. By integrating this system with an obstacle avoidance mechanism, the platform can autonomously navigate and perform task-specific path following while avoiding detected obstacles within a predefined safety margin. The effectiveness of the system is demonstrated through simulation studies on a virtual platform and real-world tests on an unmanned surface vehicle, showcasing its effectiveness in flexible navigation and safe obstacle avoidance within the specified parameters.

Nereid, the most distant known satellite in the Solar System, possesses the least understood surface composition of any object beyond Neptune. Its highly eccentric orbit leads to significant tidal heating, resulting in surface temperatures that vary widely. Although spectroscopic analysis from the Hubble Space Telescope and Hubble and Keck telescopes combined, has identified surface ices of N2 and CH4 and dust particles on the surface of Nereid, the spectral data obtained so far have been too limited and affected by a low signal-to-noise ratio to fully explain the surface composition of this distant object. 

Our research presents a high-resolution, visible spectrum of Nereid with a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 40 between 0.43 and 0.5 micrometers, outside of the Hubble UV spectrum's range. Our analysis detected a Harkins feature in Nereid's spectrum at approximately 0.48 micrometers, suggesting a surface composition of N2-CH4 icy mix, similar to other trans-Neptunian objects such as Pluto and TNO 2013 MT69. 

Our results also indicate that Nereid's surface might be subject to some degree of maceration or processing, potentially caused by cosmic ray bombardment or methanogenesis. Our spectral analysis further suggests that Nereid's surface is relatively dark and free from tholins, and that its surface composition is consistent with a N2-

We establish that any affine plane, derived from a projective line based on a set of elements, can be expanded into a comprehensive projective plane. Notably, this result diverges from findings in finite geometry, where such a promotion is not always feasible. Our work also provides a parametric model for sets of parallel lines within the affine plane, effectively trimming a collection of lines from the extended plane. We further illustrate that the group of automorphisms of the projective plane bears a direct relationship to the algebraic structure of the defining set of elements. Our findings encompass and generalize a previously published study by De Wolff.

The introduction of C. Henle, J. Sharpe, and B. Weyler's concept of Tukey-order with multiple models has opened up a range of new research possibilities. We explore this order's capabilities for establishing connections between various cardinal characteristics of the real numbers. Building upon their initial finding that it can be used to demonstrate $\mathfrak{b}\leq\mathfrak{c}_{\mathrm{H}}$, we provide more extensive evidence and additional examples showing its utility in implying other cardinal characteristic relationships. Furthermore, in contrast to previous methods requiring a Lebesgue measure 0 set, we one case provide an approach requiring only a meager set.

This research addresses the issue of creating an optimal dynamic treatment policy in a general context. We introduce a novel application of the pessimism principle in conjunction with Thompson sampling, and demonstrate that this approach allows a learner to learn a nearly optimal policy using minimal prior knowledge. Furthermore, we implement a practical version of the method and find that it outperforms existing techniques in several statistical models by a significant margin.

We prove invariance of certain higher algebraic K-groups when passing to specific subcategories of finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring, specifically those subcategories generated by a single module through set-theoretic operations. This finding has significant implications for computing the higher algebraic K-groups of Dedekind domains with finite class numbers and smooth schemes.

A novel method is proposed to connect various configurations of quantum systems through concepts of nonlocality and contextuality, offering two key outcomes. Firstly, a quantitative measure is established for the maximum local value achievable by a subset of quantum states within a particular configuration, enabling control and optimization of contextuality and nonlocality in device-independent protocols. This control can lead to a range of configurations exhibiting various levels of nonlocal or contextual behavior. Secondly, a contextuality threshold is set, above which any quantum state will be contextually related to at least one pure state, providing a boundary for the set of non-contextual quantum states. Similarly, a nonlocality threshold is defined, above which any quantum state will be nonlocality-related to at least one mixed state. The proposed framework offers valuable insights and tools for further investigation in the fields of nonlocality and contextuality.

In multi-band Hubbard models with degenerate orbitals, we find that for a large number of orbitals, the strongest pairing is most pronounced at specific conditions. A key factor is the presence of exact ground states with only one electron per orbital, which is similar to the case of $d$-wave pairing in Hubbard-Hamiltonian on square lattice with only one orbital per site. We demonstrate that when this condition is met, the wave function can be written as a product of orbital-specific components. This leads to the pairing within each orbital being significantly stronger than when the condition is not met. We also show that the pairing within each orbital can be represented in a simple and intuitive way. Finally, we establish a lower bound for the pairing within each orbital.

This work addresses two critical challenges related to $a$-adic solenoids, a branch of $p$-adic analysis. Firstly, we find solutions to the functional equation $\Phi(ax) = \sum_{k=0}^{b-1} c_k \Phi(x-c_k)$ on these structures, employing both meromorphic functions on the complex plane and continuous functions. Secondly, we address the generalized Pólya theorem for the $a$-adic solenoid by establishing connections to boundary value problems with support constraints.

Cluster analysis has been utilized for various tasks such as categorizing biological entities and identifying patterns in data.  When working with presence-absence data, researchers have employed cluster analysis using algorithms and similarity measures appropriate for this data type.  This study reviews and compares four methods for categorizing biological entities based on presence-absence data: correspondence analysis, the Gower distance, the Jaccard distance, and a methods that involves a model-based approach known as thresholding.
